done_when.text: A week later, with your notes hidden, you can name the occupant's job or habits from the props in your room drawing; showing someone is optional
Extended with a ruler, a street scene's receding lines meet their vanishing points within about 1 cm on A4, and the scene has at least two scale cues such as doors, people or vehicles

revisit.title: Invented place, cold
revisit.description: From a one-line place you have not drawn (a ferry waiting room, a canyon bridge), make a five-minute three-value thumbnail, then a quick two-point block-in with one doorway and one person for scale.

@des-visual-storytelling.p0.description: Design a single image that implies what happened just before and what will happen next (a tipped chair, muddy footprints, an open window). Do three versions. Hide your notes, and a week later write what you think happened; asking a friend is optional.

add_practice.title: Letter one panel
add_practice.description: Take one panel of your comic and add a speech balloon and a caption by hand. Write the text first in even capitals, then draw the balloon around it with the tail pointing at the speaker's mouth, and place balloons so they read from top left in order.

done_when.text: For three single images, a week later with your notes hidden, you can still read from the clues what happened before and what happens next; showing someone is optional
Your silent four-panel comic shows its change or reveal in the last panel without words, and a week later you can read the story from the panels alone

revisit.title: Before and after, cold
revisit.description: Pick a moment you have not drawn (a dropped tray, an empty birdcage). Draw one image that implies before and after, then two thumbnails of the same moment at different shot sizes, and note which tells it better.

landscape-elements-and-trees.summary: Natural elements without a fixed shape need rules instead of outlines: rocks as a few planes, mountains as layered masses, clouds as lit volumes, water as reflection and movement, fire and smoke as flowing shapes, and trees as masses and silhouettes rather than leaves. You practise each element alone, then combine them in layered scenes under one light. Free teaching is thin for rocks, fire and smoke, so the lesson notes cover those.

resources.notes: John Muir Laws's landscape pages: clouds ('How to Draw Cloud Shapes', then clouds in perspective), water (creeks and moving water, open ocean) and trees (deciduous trees, oaks, aspens, coniferous forests). Draw along with each.

done_when.text: Photographed in greyscale, a forest scene shows at least three separate value layers

revisit.title: Rock, cloud and tree
revisit.description: From imagination, draw one rock as four planes under a stated light, one cumulus cloud with a lit side, and one tree as a silhouette of three to five clumps, then check each against a photo.

architecture-and-slopes.summary: Buildings are boxes in perspective with roofs, openings and repeated parts, and roofs, ramps, stairs and hillside streets add sloped lines whose vanishing points sit above or below the horizon. You learn roof types, windows and doors that shrink correctly, wall thickness, arches in perspective, and the construction for inclines, each taught where you use it.

resources.notes: Studio Chalkboard lesson 10, 'Inclines: finding roof pitches and declines'. Redraw its constructions before the roof and ramp exercises.
Book II covers uneven ground and descending planes; Book III covers roofs, arches, stairs and winding stairs. Read selected chapters for the geometry.

practice.title: Ramp check in the form viewer
practice.description: Build the ramp or stair as a box in the form viewer and orbit to your drawing's viewpoint. The ramp's sloped edge runs from the box's bottom front edge to its top back edge; check that its vanishing point sits on the vertical line through the flat box's vanishing point.

done_when.text: Extended with a ruler, every set of horizontal edges on one building meets its vanishing point within about 1 cm on A4
Extended with a ruler, the sloped edges of a roof or ramp meet at a point on the vertical line through the flat vanishing point, within about 1 cm on A4

revisit.title: House on a slope
revisit.description: Draw a two-point house with a gabled roof standing at the side of a street that runs uphill, with two windows and a door showing wall thickness. Extend the roof and street lines to check their vanishing points.

location-and-street-sketching.summary: Location sketching applies observation under time pressure: you decide what the sketch is about, put the big shapes down first, simplify hard and accept a loose result. You work in five-minute street series, quick people in cafes, inventories of street clutter at the right scale, and a 30-minute scene now and then, building the visual library from life. It opens once block-in and composition are in place and runs as an ongoing habit.

practice.dose: 10 sketches over two outings, 5 min each

done_when.text: You have completed four 30-minute scenes on location, any spacing
Timed, you can simplify a busy street into a few large shapes in under five minutes

revisit.title: Five-minute corner
revisit.description: At a window or on a street you have not drawn, decide in one sentence what the sketch is about, then do a five-minute sketch with the big shapes first. Add two people as simple shapes for scale.

@persp-scene-capstone.p1.dose: 1 drawing, about 3 hours over two or three sessions

@persp-scene-capstone.p2.dose: 1 drawing, about 4 hours over several sessions

@persp-scene-capstone.p3.dose: 1 drawing, about 4 hours over several sessions

@persp-scene-capstone.p4.description: After each drawing, extend its main lines on a copy and write three sentences naming three construction errors and what you would change. Redraw one corner of the picture to fix one of them.

done_when.text: On a flat floor, the horizon cuts every same-height figure at the same body point in each scene, checked with a ruler

revisit.title: Room with three people
revisit.description: Draw a quick one-point room you have not drawn with three same-height people at different distances and one window shadow, then check the horizon cuts each person at the same height.
